open_points.subject: Persistence of run-derived StoredValues
open_points.text: “`run_values` for the values a run derives for delivery ... always through `store.put_value_bytes`” contradicts “`run_values.deliver_input`, which writes what the source still needs written through `store.record_change`” and “writing each through `store.record_change`”.
open_points.question: Which store capability writes the StoredValue record and its bytes for a run-derived value, and are those writes one transaction or separate operations?
options: `put_value_bytes` writes the bytes, then `record_change` inserts the StoredValue record
`record_change` writes both the bytes and the StoredValue record
`put_value_bytes` alone writes both, and `deliver_input` does not call `record_change` for the value
open_points.default_guess: Use `put_value_bytes` to publish/deduplicate bytes and `record_change` to insert the StoredValue record before validation.

open_points.subject: Mapped empty-list StoredValue
open_points.text: “StoredValue M21 and value bytes are written by ... `run_values` for the values a run derives for delivery” conflicts with “The empty list of a mapped node over an empty list is built by `run_values.empty_list_outputs` and written by `runs` with the node's one NodeExecution”.
open_points.question: Which module owns and writes the StoredValue record and bytes for mapped-node empty-list outputs?
options: `runs` writes the StoredValue and NodeExecution together from data built by `run_values`
`run_values` writes the StoredValue before `runs` writes the NodeExecution
`run_values` writes the bytes, while `runs` inserts the StoredValue record with the NodeExecution
open_points.default_guess: Have `run_values` build the canonical bytes and metadata, while `runs` writes the StoredValue record and NodeExecution in the same store change.

open_points.subject: Access to the complete run trace
open_points.text: “`runs` ... passes the graph, those ports and the run's trace to `run_graph`” is not reconciled with “A module reads what a module it may know owns through that module's capability, and never decides from another module's raw records” and the fact that operation NodeExecutions are written by `effects`.
open_points.question: Which module owns and exposes the complete ordered trace, including operation NodeExecutions, so that `runs` can pass it to `run_graph` without reading another module's raw records?
options: `runs` owns the aggregate trace and may read every NodeExecution through `store`
`effects` exposes operation NodeExecutions through a new read capability and `runs` combines them with its records
`run_graph` obtains operation records through an expanded `effects` capability instead of receiving a complete trace
open_points.default_guess: Treat `runs` as owner of the aggregate trace and explicitly permit it to read all NodeExecution records through `store`, while `effects` remains their transactional writer.

open_points.subject: Failure caused by an oversized mapped output list
open_points.text: “a list over it fails the node with no record” is assigned no single owner: `run_values` “Must not own ... what ... a list over the ceiling concludes ... (`run_graph`, `runs`)”; `run_graph` owns only “A13 rules 2, 4, 5, 7 and 8”; and `runs` “Must not own ... propagation or the run's derived status (`run_graph`)”.
open_points.question: Which module decides that an oversized assembled mapped list makes the mapped node failed and derives its downstream and run consequences?
options: `run_graph` owns the derived failure and its propagation; `run_values` only reports the measurement result
`runs` converts the measurement result into a node failure before asking `run_graph` to propagate it
`run_values` returns a domain-level failed-node conclusion that `run_graph` consumes
open_points.default_guess: Make `run_graph` the sole owner of the derived mapped-node failure and its propagation, with `run_values` returning only the measured over-ceiling result.

open_points.subject: Recovery when one wait is resolved but another remains
open_points.text: “a run that still waits is not advanced: only its lagging status and waiting points are rewritten ... and no element is reached” conflicts with A13 rule 8, “While some elements wait, every other ready node keeps executing”, when recovery observes one resolved waiting element that makes work ready while another element still waits.
open_points.question: At startup, if resolving or deciding one stored wait makes an element or its dependants ready but another waiting point remains, must recovery advance that ready work or leave the whole run unadvanced?
options: Advance all ready work while preserving the remaining waits, as A13 rule 8 requires
Do not advance any run that retains at least one waiting point
Advance only the element whose former waiting point was resolved, then stop if another wait remains
open_points.default_guess: Advance all newly ready work and retain the unrelated waiting points; stop only when no element can execute.
